stories.headline: Lt Gen Mohit Seth takes over as White Knight Corps Commander
stories.title: Lt Gen Mohit Seth takes over as White Knight Corps Commander
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 1: Lieutenant General Mohit Seth, SM, VSM on Thursday took over as the Commander of the White Knight Corps from Lieutenant General P K Mishra, UYSM, AVSM, YSM, SM. Lt Gen Seth assumed command of the Corps and exhorted all ranks to maintain the highest standards of operational readiness, professional excellence and team spirit. He also called upon the troops to continue contributing towards peace, security and stability in the region. The Army, in a statement, said the new Corps Commander emphasised the need for sustained preparedness and collective commitment in carrying out operational responsibilities. The White Knight Corps is responsible for military operations in the Jammu region, including areas along the Line of Control. “Prepared for today. Ready for tomorrow,” the Army said, reiterating its commitment to serving and protecting the region. Lt Gen P K Mishra’s tenure as White Knight Corps commander lasted 18 months, from April 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026. He took over from Lt Gen Navin Sachdeva and was succeeded by Lt Gen Mohit Seth. Mishra’s tenure coincided with several significant security developments in the Jammu region, including heightened counter-terror operations following the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The White Knight Corps also maintained a sustained focus on counter-infiltration operations along the Line of Control and counter-terror operations in the Pir Panjal and Chenab valley regions. During his tenure, Mishra regularly reviewed operations in Doda, Kishtwar, Udhampur, Rajouri and Poonch. In September 2025, he reviewed ongoing anti-terror operations in the hilly areas of Udhampur, Doda and Kishtwar following encounters with terrorists. In 2026, his focus also included strengthening technological and air-defence capabilities. In May, he reviewed air-defence preparedness, counter-drone capabilities and security along the LoC in Rajouri. In one of his final operational visits as Corps Commander, Mishra visited Surankote in Poonch in September 2026 to review the security situation and focused counter-terror operations, including efforts to dominate the Pir Panjal Range. Mishra, who was earlier Commandant of the Indian Military Training Team (IMTRAT) in Bhutan, was awarded the Uttam Yudh Seva Medal in 2026.

stories.summary: State Cabinet decided to convene an all-party meeting soon and hold consultations with farmers’ associations and experts from different sectors before finalising the mitigation measures as the State recorded a rainfall deficit of about 17% during the monsoon, which ended on Wednesday, the Minister for Information Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy said

article_sentences: The State Cabinet has approved the release of two pending instaments of Dearness Allowance (DAs) to government employees and pensioners, said Minister for Revenue, Housing and Information and Public Relations Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy.
“The Cabinet also decided to constitute a sub-committee to examine immediate measures to be taken in areas affected by the El Niño conditions.
It also resolved to convene an all-party meeting soon and hold consultations with farmers’ associations and experts from different sectors before finalising the mitigation measures.
The State government would also seek the Centre’s assistance and request the declaration of drought-affected areas,” he added.
Briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister.

A. Revanth Reddy at the Secretariat here on Thursday, the Minister said the two DAs would be released immediately from among the arrears pending since 2024, while the remaining arrears would be cleared in instalments.
“The release of DAs will impose an additional annual financial burden of about ₹2,500 crore on the State government.
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has decided to release the DA despite the financial burden, in line with the assurance given during recent discussions with employee unions,” he said.
The Cabinet also discussed the El Nino conditions and the deficient monsoon in the State.
Mr. Srinivasa Reddy said Telangana had recorded a rainfall deficit of about 17% during the monsoon, which ended on Wednesday.
The Cabinet also decided to make arrangements for procurement of paddy during the kharif season.
On power supply, Mr. Srinivasa Reddy said electricity consumption had increased significantly amid the prevailing conditions.

stories.headline: The Political Monopoly of the National Conference in J&K Must End
stories.title: The Political Monopoly of the National Conference in J&K Must End
stories.summary: For decades, Jammu Kashmir—particularly the Kashmir Valley—has witnessed the extraordinary persistence of one political idea: that the National Conference (NC) is indispensable to the region's political identity and democratic equilibrium. The party has surely played a major role in the political history of Jammu Kashmir. But historical importance cannot become a permanent claim to political ownership, particularly when its record is full of blemishes. In a democracy, no party, family or political tradition can legitimately claim that it alone represents the aspirations of an entire people. The question, therefore, is whether NC’s historical legacy should confer upon it a special political status that places it above ordinary democratic competition. The history of dissent cannot be ignored The history of Jammu and Kashmir contains numerous episodes that raise difficult questions about the treatment of political dissent and electoral competition. The political career of journalist-politician Shamim Ahmed Shamim is particularly relevant to this discussion. A celebrated Urdu journalist, editor of Aina, powerful orator and former Member of Parliament, Shamim was at one stage associated with Sheikh Abdullah but later became a fierce critic of his government and the National Conference establishment. Shamim attacked what he regarded as the concentration of political authority around one leader and one party. His criticism was not simply electoral; he challenged the political culture that, in his view, left insufficient space for independent democratic alternatives. He believed “Wahid Party" (Single Party) and "Wahid Leader" (Single Leader) syndrome was fascist. Accounts of his conflicts with the administration—including legal disputes, pressure on his newspaper and restrictions on his political activity—remain an important part of the history of dissent in Kashmir. Contemporary reporting also documented restrictions imposed on him during the late 1970s, when Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah returned to power as a Chief Minister. These episodes deserve examination not as isolated political quarrels but as part of the larger question of how dissent was accommodated by the political establishment of the time. The significance of Shamim's story lies precisely here: democratic institutions are tested not when everyone agrees with the government, but when an influential citizen challenges the dominant political narrative. His experience also demonstrates why political legitimacy cannot be inherited. A political leader may once be an ally and later become a critic. A journalist may become a politician. A regional voice may cooperate with a national political formation. None of these choices should make a citizen less entitled to participate in democratic politics. But the NC narrative with respect to Shamim Sahab shifted from viewing him as a "modern voice of Kashmir" to treating him as a traitor to the regional cause, the moment he independent-mindedly aligned with national democratic alternatives—like the Janata Party—to build a viable local opposition. The unresolved questions surrounding 1951 and 1987 The NC's historical record is often invoked as evidence of its unparalleled popular legitimacy. The party won all 75 seats in the 1951 Jammu and Kashmir Constituent Assembly elections. Yet the circumstances surrounding those elections—including the rejection of opposition nominations even in Kashmir and the absence of meaningful electoral competition—have long been examined critically by historians and political scholars. A complete electoral sweep cannot automatically be equated with an uncomplicated democratic mandate when meaningful competition is absent or suppressed. The 1987 Assembly elections present an even more consequential example. Allegations of electoral malpractice and the subsequent political consequences have been extensively discussed in scholarship on the origins of the crisis that followed. The NC and its allies have disputed particular interpretations of that history, but the broader lesson is difficult to avoid: public confidence in elections is itself a democratic institution, and once citizens lose faith in the electoral process, the consequences can extend far beyond one election. The purpose of revisiting these episodes should not be to delegitimise the NC or any other group as a political party. It should be to establish a democratic principle: no party should be above scrutiny simply because it possesses a long history. Kashmir's political space is larger than one party The NC has never possessed a permanent monopoly over public opinion. Jammu and Kashmir's political landscape has included the electorally significant regional as well as national political parties, smaller regional organisations, independents and newer political formations. Their varying electoral fortunes demonstrate that political preferences are neither uniform nor permanently fixed. The claim that Kashmir must choose between political accommodation with the NC and instability creates a false binary. Citizens can simultaneously demand democratic rights, constitutional governance, development, security and political alternatives. No party should be permitted to present itself as the sole institutional bridge between citizens and the Union government. Nor should New Delhi assume that governance requires dependence upon one regional intermediary. Constitutional positions, too, have evolved Political positions in Jammu and Kashmir have never been frozen in time. This is also evident in the changing positions historically associated with Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah and the constitutional relationship between New Delhi and Srinagar. A March 13, 1981 report in Kashmir Times, for example, recorded Sheikh Abdullah discussing Article 370 as something that was not necessarily immutable. The report recorded Sheikh saying that Article 370 was “not sacrosanct” and could be altered or abrogated. Whatever one's interpretation of that statement, the historical point is important: political positions evolve. Constitutional arrangements evolve. Parties evolve. Governments change. Leaders alter their positions. What should not change is the democratic right of citizens to question their representatives and replace them through peaceful elections. Breaking the politics of dependency The political and administrative developments since 2019 have demonstrated that citizens can interact with the state through institutions beyond traditional regional political intermediaries. Local self-government, Panchayati Raj institutions, urban local bodies, elected representatives and direct administrative mechanisms provide additional channels through which citizens can participate in governance. The strengthening of these institutions should not be understood as an alternative to political parties. Rather, it reduces the danger of concentrating political representation in a single intermediary, “Wahid Party" (Single Party) and "Wahid Leader" (Single Leader) . No persecution. No privilege. No monopoly. The objective should not be to replace one political monopoly with another. The National Conference must have the same democratic rights as every other political party—and the same democratic obligations. It should neither be persecuted nor privileged. It should be free to contest elections, campaign, criticise governments and seek public support. But it must also be prepared to defend its record, answer criticism and accept electoral defeat when voters choose an alternative. The same standard must apply to every other party. A genuinely democratic Jammu and Kashmir must also guarantee a political environment in which citizens can express disagreement without intimidation, violence, coercion, social ostracisation or organised campaigns of vilification. Political disagreement must remain political disagreement—not become a reason for threats or punishment. The people of Kashmir do not need a permanent political intermediary. They need accountable representatives. They do not need a political dynasty to speak permanently on their behalf. They need institutions through which they can speak for themselves. New Delhi, likewise, need not choose between dependence on one regional party and direct central administration. The durable alternative is stronger elected institutions, empowered local government, civil society and genuinely competitive politics. The ultimate antidote to the doctrine of political indispensability is not another doctrine. It is democracy itself. A Jammu and Kashmir in which the National Conference is neither persecuted nor privileged; in which it must earn every vote, defend every policy, answer for its record and accept the verdict of the electorate like every other political party—that is not the destruction of democracy. It is democracy functioning as it should. No party owns Kashmir's political space. No more “Wahid Party" and "Wahid Leader" . (The Author is a former Member of the Legislative Council of Jammu and Kashmir and spokesperson of BJP JK-UT)

stories.title: Manipur Cabinet approves Rs 10 lakh aid for kin of 49 missing since 2023 violence
stories.summary: Manipur Cabinet approves Rs 10 lakh aid for kin of 49 missing since 2023 violence
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
event term: 'cabinet approves' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Manipur Cabinet has approved Rs 10 lakh each for the families of 49 people still missing since the May 2023 violence.
The meeting also cleared higher ex-gratia for security personnel, a pension rise for retired journalists and the Fifth State Finance Commission.

The Manipur Cabinet on Thursday approved a one-time special humanitarian assistance of Rs 10 lakh each for the next of kin of 49 people who have remained missing since the violence that erupted in the state on May 3, 2023.
The 49 people remain untraced despite sustained search efforts.
The total financial implication of the assistance will be Rs 4.90 crore, which will be borne by the Manipur government.
The decision was among four key measures approved at the state Cabinet meeting held on Thursday.
The Cabinet also approved revised ex-gratia compensation for Army and Central Armed.
Police Forces (CAPF) personnel killed or injured in extremist violence or related actions while operating in Manipur.

Under the revised rates, Rs 10 lakh will be provided in case of death, while compensation for injuries has been fixed at Rs 2 lakh for permanent disability, Rs 1 lakh for grievous injury and Rs 20,000 for simple injury.
The earlier ex-gratia compensation was Rs 2 lakh in case of death and Rs 10,000 for injuries.
These rates had been fixed in 2006.
The Cabinet also approved an increase in the monthly pension for retired journalists under the Manipur Working Journalists' Pension Rules, 1996.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 1, 2026) stayed the execution of the death sentence awarded to an Indian Mujahideen operative in the 2008 Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts case, in which 56 people were killed.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, A.G. Masih and Sandeep Mehta passed the interim order while hearing an appeal filed by Ahmed Bawa, alias Abbu Abubakar Barelvi, challenging the Gujarat High Court verdict affirming the death sentence imposed on him by the trial court.
The Bench issued notice to the Gujarat government and called for the trial court records, while directing that the death sentence not be executed in the meantime.
Appearing for Barelvi, his counsel contended that his conviction rested entirely on the allegation that he was part of the conspiracy behind the blasts.
“I have been convicted totally on the basis of conspiracy,” the counsel submitted.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Gujarat government, however, opposed the plea, stressing the gravity of the case.
“It is a serious case,” Mr. Mehta submitted.
On July 26, 2008, a series of 21 bomb blasts ripped through Ahmedabad within a span of 70 minutes, killing 56 people and injuring more than 200.
Explosions also occurred at hospitals where victims of the attacks were being taken for treatment.
On July 7, the Gujarat High Court upheld the death sentences awarded to 38 convicts in the case and the life sentences imposed on 11 others.

While upholding the capital punishment, the High Court cited the scale of the casualties, the “humongous nature of conspiracy” and the intention “to create an atmosphere of widespread terror in the society”.
It also took into account the roles and criminal antecedents of the convicts and their conduct during the trial.

Appearing for Barelvi, his counsel contended that his conviction rested entirely on the allegation that he was part of the conspiracy behind the blasts.
“I have been convicted totally on the basis of conspiracy,” the counsel submitted.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Gujarat government, however, opposed the plea, stressing the gravity of the case.
“It is a serious case,” Mr. Mehta submitted.
On July 26, 2008, a series of 21 bomb blasts ripped through Ahmedabad within a span of 70 minutes, killing 56 people and injuring more than 200.
Explosions also occurred at hospitals where victims of the attacks were being taken for treatment.
On July 7, the Gujarat High Court upheld the death sentences awarded to 38 convicts in the case and the life sentences imposed on 11 others.

India and Pakistan will meet in the group stage of the 2027 ODI World Cup, with defending champions Australia also drawn into the same group for the tournament in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
The ICC revealed the 14-team World Cup groups on Thursday at the schedule launch in Cape Town, confirming a heavyweight Group.
A featuring India, Pakistan, Australia, Afghanistan, co-hosts Zimbabwe and the winner of Qualifier.
For cricket fans, the draw guarantees another India-Pakistan contest on the biggest stage.
India currently top the ODI rankings, while Shubman Gill will lead the team at his first ODI World Cup.
Who is in each World Cup group?
Ten teams have already qualified directly for the tournament.
They are India, Pakistan, Australia, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, England, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, South Africa and Zimbabwe.
The remaining places will be decided through the qualification process, with the final entrant into the main tournament coming from a new pre-tournament contest.
When will the 2027 ODI World Cup begin?
The World Cup will start on October 2, 2027, with the final scheduled for November 21.

stories.headline: NCLT approves Tata Steel merger with wholly owned subsidiary
stories.title: NCLT approves Tata Steel merger with wholly owned subsidiary
stories.summary: The Mumbai Bench of the tribunal has sanctioned Tata Steel’s amalgamation with Rujuvalika Investments, clearing the scheme proposed in 2024.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai Bench, has approved and sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation between Tata Steel and its wholly owned subsidiary Rujuvalika Investments Ltd, along with their respective shareholders.
Tata Steel said the NCLT pronounced its order on October 1, 2026.
The scheme was proposed under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.
With the tribunal's order, the scheme of amalgamation has been approved and sanctioned, the company said.
The disclosure follows Tata Steel's earlier announcement dated July 31, 2024, regarding the proposed amalgamation.
The company has also submitted a copy of the NCLT order, as uploaded on the tribunal's website, to the stock exchanges.

In a separate development, Tata Steel had on Tuesday said it received a favourable order from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) in a tax dispute, allowing its claim for deduction of interest expenditure.
The company said the order would reduce its tax exposure in the matter by around ₹427 crore, from ₹1,901 crore to ₹1,474 crore.
Separately, Tata Steel said it had received a favourable order dated February 20, 2026, from the relevant authority for FY2008, allowing its claim for deduction of interest expenditure.
The company said the tax exposure for FY2008 was ₹215 crore.
The company said it had made the required disclosure to the stock exchanges on February 28, 2026.
Following that order, Tata Steel said its tax exposure for FY2008 would fall from ₹1,901 crore to ₹1,686 crore, once the Assessing Officer gives effect to the order through a consequential order.
